q1.question:
Similar to the Unix Philosophy, object-oriented programming is centered around four tenets. Match the descriptions below to the corresponding principle:

  1. This principle focuses on hiding implementation details and exposing only the essential functionality of an object.

  2. This principle encourages bundling data (attributes) and behaviors (methods) to create a cohesive unit.

  3. This principle allows treating objects of different types as instances of the same base type, as long as they implement a common interface or behavior.

  4. This principle enables creation hierarchical relationships between units to allow for code reuse.
